mil3.1.13:1.3: “Mindfulness, Great King, has the characteristic of reminding, and the characteristic of taking up.”
mil3.1.13:1.4: “How, venerable sir, does mindfulness have the characteristic of reminding?”
mil3.1.13:1.5: “Mindfulness, Great King, when it arises, reminds one of the qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright, together with their counterparts: ‘These are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, these are the four right efforts, these are the four bases of psychic power, these are the five faculties, these are the five powers, these are the seven awakening factors, this is the noble eightfold path, this is serenity, this is discernment, this is knowledge, this is freedom.’
mil3.1.13:1.6: Then the meditator makes use of the qualities that should be made use of, and does not make use of the qualities that should not be made use of.
mil3.1.13:1.7: He resorts to the qualities that should be resorted to, and does not resort to the qualities that should not be resorted to.
mil3.1.13:1.8: That, Great King, is how mindfulness has the characteristic of reminding.”
mil3.1.13:2.2: “Just as, Great King, the treasurer of a wheel-turning king reminds the wheel-turning king of his glory morning and evening: ‘So many elephants have you, Your Majesty, so many horses, so many chariots, so many foot soldiers, so much money, so much gold, so much wealth; may Your Majesty remember it’—so he reminds the king of his wealth;
mil3.1.13:2.3: so too, Great King, mindfulness, when it arises, reminds one of the qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright, together with their counterparts: ‘These are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, these are the four right efforts, these are the four bases of psychic power, these are the five faculties, these are the five powers, these are the seven awakening factors, this is the noble eightfold path, this is serenity, this is discernment, this is knowledge, this is freedom.’
mil3.1.13:2.4: Then the meditator makes use of the qualities that should be made use of, and does not make use of the qualities that should not be made use of.
mil3.1.13:2.5: He resorts to the qualities that should be resorted to, and does not resort to the qualities that should not be resorted to.
mil3.1.13:2.6: That, Great King, is how mindfulness has the characteristic of reminding.”
mil3.1.13:3.1: “How, venerable sir, does mindfulness have the characteristic of taking up?”
mil3.1.13:3.2: “Mindfulness, Great King, when it arises, follows the courses of beneficial and unbeneficial qualities: ‘These qualities are beneficial, these qualities are unbeneficial.
mil3.1.13:3.3: These qualities are helpful, these qualities are unhelpful.’
mil3.1.13:3.4: Then the meditator rejects the unbeneficial qualities and takes up the beneficial qualities.
mil3.1.13:3.5: He rejects the unhelpful qualities and takes up the helpful qualities.
mil3.1.13:3.6: That, Great King, is how mindfulness has the characteristic of taking up.”
mil3.1.13:4.2: “Just as, Great King, the commander-treasure of a wheel-turning king knows what is beneficial and unbeneficial for the king: ‘These are beneficial for the king, these are unbeneficial.
mil3.1.13:4.5: He rejects what is unhelpful and takes up what is helpful.
mil3.1.13:4.6: So too, Great King, mindfulness, when it arises, follows the courses of beneficial and unbeneficial qualities: ‘These qualities are beneficial, these qualities are unbeneficial.
mil3.1.13:4.7: These qualities are helpful, these qualities are unhelpful.’
mil3.1.13:4.8: Then the meditator rejects the unbeneficial qualities and takes up the beneficial qualities.
mil3.1.13:4.9: He rejects the unhelpful qualities and takes up the helpful qualities.
mil3.1.13:4.10: That, Great King, is how mindfulness has the characteristic of taking up.
mil3.1.13:4.12: ‘And mindfulness, mendicants, I declare to be useful everywhere.’”
